category_title: Students who feel misunderstood and engage in off-task social behavior during tutoring
minimal_context: Beaumont is attending an after-school math tutoring session to copy class notes and complete his math work.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Beaumont, it is time to start. Please take out your math assignment and copy the notes from class today.

STUDENT: I don't have my math notebook with me. Let me just look through my backpack to find a pencil and some paper so I can get ready.

TUTOR: Okay, please find what you need and begin.

STUDENT: I usually don’t know what is happening a lot during class anyway because I am kinda late usually or not paying attention. I learn differently.

TUTOR: Just try to focus on the math work right now.

STUDENT: (Turns to the student at the next desk) Hey, what are you working on? Look at this. I know I just have to stop messing around when I go, but I'm still preparing my stuff. My teacher doesn’t help the ones that are screwing around anyway – I get kicked out a lot [laughing].

options.A: Give the student only one-step directions for copying the math notes.
options.B: Sit with the student and discuss personal interests like college basketball.
options.C: Give the student single-digit addition problems while everyone else does two-digit addition.
options.D: Directly intervene and tell the nearby peers that they need to stop.
